source.title: ConTrans: Weak-to-Strong Alignment Engineering via Concept Transplantation
source.authors: Weilong Dong; Xinwei Wu; Ren-Ren Jin; Shao-Yang Xu; De-Yi Xiong

page_placements.theme: Decoding-, logit- or activation-level guidance of a frozen stronger model by smaller models (proxy-tuning, reward-guided decoding, steering vectors)

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites weak-to-strong supervision and develops concept transplantation as an alternative alignment method. It reports outcomes for that method, not results from fine-tuning a strong student on weak-model labels or measuring PGR.
record.gate_note: The reported transfer results use activation-space concept vectors and deliberately steer the target model. They are related to weak-to-strong alignment, but do not measure the label-supervised training effect or performance gap recovered in the claim versions. The paper also reports emotion-transplantation, PPL, and additional ablation and vector-source results; these do not test any listed version. Rows below capture the main numerical truthfulness and toxicity transfer results and the reported truthfulness comparisons across source vectors.
record.test_reason: ConTrans adds concept vectors taken from a 7B aligned model into the residual stream of larger base models. That is a deliberately induced activation-steering intervention. No strong model is fine-tuned on weak-model labels, and no weak-supervisor baseline, strong ceiling or PGR is reported, so no version of the claim is tested. Burns et al. is cited only as motivation, and the paper does not rely on its finding as a tool. That makes this discussion (T6) rather than use-as-tool (T4), though T4 is arguable.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors conclude that transferable shared concept features let vectors refined from weak aligned models steer strong base models without training. They present this as an internal, hidden-space alternative to weak-to-strong supervision.
record.recipe_differences: The original method fine-tunes a strong model on labels synthesized by a weak model and measures PGR. This paper extracts concept vectors from a source model, reformulates them with an affine transformation, and adds them to a target model's residual stream. No weak-label student training or PGR is used.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that transfer effectiveness depends on source/target architecture and pretraining-data similarity; concept expression varies with pretraining scale and alignment stage. Steering strength also changes emotion prediction accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Concept vectors from 7B instruct models, added to 13B/70B base models, raise TruthfulQA MC1 accuracy (e.g. LLaMA 2-13B 17.9% to 36.5%). They also cut Toxigen toxic-response rates (e.g. 91.8% to 34.1%). In some cases the steered strong model exceeds the 7B source's own accuracy (Code LLaMA-70B 33.4% vs 7B-instruct 29.3%, Table 6). Vectors from base models help less.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-space concept vectors from a smaller aligned model can steer a larger base model toward alignment-related outputs without training, with effectiveness depending on source-target similarity.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the listed results. Toxicity evaluation uses 200 evaluation samples per Toxigen group, and the intervention strength is selected using a validation set of 10 samples per group. The intervention intentionally steers outputs, so its results do not show the uninduced weak-to-strong fine-tuning effect in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's emotion-transfer experiments and PCA visualizations, PPL comparisons, and supplementary transfer tables (including Table 6 and Table 10) are not catalogued as rows because they report activation-transplantation behavior or auxiliary measures rather than any listed claim version. Table 1 and Table 2 baseline comparator methods are not separate rows because the rows record the concept-transplantation intervention outcomes.

untested.parts: No strong student is trained on weak labels; no PGR or weak-supervisor-versus-student comparison under label supervision.
No auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling or loss variants applied to weak-label fine-tuning.
The size and representation results (Pythia grid, Amber checkpoints) concern steering-vector transfer, not PGR.
No weak-label fine-tuning failure modes tested.
No theory of when a student must beat its supervisor.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation was changed from uses_without_test/T4 to discusses/T6, because the paper does not use the Burns finding as a tool. All rows are correctly linked to none. The 'weak-to-strong' label here refers to steering, not label supervision, so no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No strong model is fine-tuned on labels produced by a weak supervisor; no weak-supervisor score or PGR is reported for that procedure.
No auxiliary confidence loss, weak-supervisor ensembling, or loss variant is compared with naive weak-label fine-tuning.
The paper studies model sizes, tasks, and representations for activation-vector transplantation, not PGR variation under weak-label fine-tuning.
No weak-label fine-tuning failure modes, distribution-shift effects on PGR, or error-overlap effects are tested.
No theory of when a student must beat a weak supervisor is tested or developed.
The experiments are on language models; no vision experiment is reported.

relation.reason: The introduction and related work discuss weak-label supervision and motivate an alternative intervention in hidden representations; the experiments do not test the catalog's claim versions.

tranche.reason: The experiments evaluate concept-vector transplantation rather than strong-model fine-tuning on weak labels. They neither test a listed claim version nor use the established weak-label generalization effect as a tool.

source_check.notes: All numerical cells and stated transfer conditions check out; retain these as related findings with versions=none. Model weights are not fine-tuned, but the affine transformation is fitted; LLaMA's table designation 70B means 65B.
